reader.decision: Do not lower the CDN TTL. Use event-driven eviction: each pod pops its own price_cache entry on price.changed. Also lower the pod ttl from 3600 to 300 as a backstop. Proceed, and wire start_invalidation() wherever shop/app.py wires search/indexer.py.
reader.decision_reason: The message says the CDN already skips /api/*, so my TTL proposal would change nothing. The staleness comes from per-pod caches that only the admin-serving pod clears. price.changed already exists, so evicting on it fixes the cause and gives consistent prices within about a second.

reconstruction.problem: Each of the 6 shop-api pods has its own in-process price_cache with ttl=3600. update_price pops the entry only in the pod that served the admin request, then publishes price.changed. Only search/indexer.py subscribes, so the other 5 pods keep the old price for up to an hour. The CDN is not involved, because cdn/rules.yaml already sets cache: false for /api/*.
reconstruction.what_breaks: After a price change, reloads return different prices depending on which pod answers (34.90 from pod A, 39.90 from pods B to F, per SM-140). Stale pods can serve the old price for up to 3600 seconds, and customers pay the old price at checkout.
reconstruction.fix: In pricing/service.py add on_price_changed(payload), which pops payload["sku"] from price_cache, and start_invalidation(), which subscribes it to price.changed. Call start_invalidation() at startup in shop/app.py. Make no CDN change. Optionally lower the pod ttl to 300 so a missed event heals sooner.
reconstruction.cost: One Redis subscription per pod. Redis pub/sub does not replay events, so a pod that misses a message keeps the old price until its ttl expires. The shop/app.py wiring location was not read and is unverified.

follow_up_questions: Does subscribe() on price.changed deliver every message to every pod (fan-out), rather than to one competing consumer? The fix depends on it, and the message only says search/indexer.py subscribes.
reader.closing_answer: Evict price_cache on price.changed in all 6 pods, not the 60-second pod TTL. I would also lower the pod ttl to 300 as a backstop for missed events. I would have Aelita confirm that subscribe() fans out to every pod when it makes the change.
